title: MARS: Systematic Multi-Level Acceleration for World Action Models
title_zh: MARS：面向世界动作模型的系统化多级加速方法

paragraphs.en: MARS提出了一种面向世界动作模型的系统化多级加速方法，显著提高了模型在高频闭环控制中的应用效率。 World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising alternative for embodied intelligence by jointly predicting future world states and robot actions. However, their heavy visual encoding and iterative generative inference incur substantial latency, limiting their applicability to high-frequency closed-loop control. Existing training-free acceleration methods typically optimize a single stage, yielding limited speedups or degraded control under aggressive reuse. In this work, we systematically profile the inference overhead of WAMs and observe abundant redundancy across Transformer computation, diffusion denoising, and consecutive policy queries. However, the safe removal of such redundancy depends strongly on its impact on action prediction and control sensitivity. Based on these observations, we introduce \textbf{MARS}, a training-free and plug-and-play framework for multi-level WAM acceleration. MARS selectively removes low-impact attention computation, adaptively accelerates diffusion inference according to motion granularity, and speculatively reuses predicted future visual representations across consecutive queries with online verification. Together, these complementary mechanisms provide remarkable acceleration while limiting approximation error. Extensive experiments across LIBERO, LIBERO-PRO, and RoboCasa show that MARS achieves up to $4.00\times$, $3.94\times$, and $2.10\times$ end-to-end speedups, respectively, while maintaining task success rate close to the original policy. Moreover, MARS generalizes across different model backbones and across simulation and real-robot experiments, substantially improving the efficiency--performance trade-off of WAM inference. Our code is available at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/MARS.
paragraphs.zh: MARS提出了一种面向世界动作模型的系统化多级加速方法，显著提高了模型在高频闭环控制中的应用效率。世界动作模型（WAMs）通过联合预测未来世界状态和机器人动作，已成为具身智能的一种有前景的替代方案。 然而，其繁重的视觉编码和迭代生成推理带来了显著的延迟，限制了其在高频闭环控制中的适用性。 现有的免训练加速方法通常仅优化单个阶段，导致加速效果有限，或在激进复用下造成控制性能下降。 在本工作中，我们系统性地分析了WAMs的推理开销，并观察到Transformer计算、扩散去噪以及连续策略查询之间存在大量冗余。 然而，安全地移除这些冗余在很大程度上取决于它们对动作预测和控制敏感性的影响。 基于这些观察结果，我们提出了\textbf{MARS}——一个免训练且即插即用的WAM多级加速框架。 MARS选择性地移除低影响的注意力计算，根据运动颗粒度自适应地加速扩散推理，并通过在线验证在连续查询中推测性复用预测的未来视觉表示。 这些互补机制共同实现了显著的加速效果，同时控制了近似误差。 在LIBERO、LIBERO-PRO和RoboCasa上的广泛实验表明，MARS分别实现了高达$4.00\times$、$3.94\times$和$2.10\times$的端到端加速，同时保持了与原始策略相近的任务成功率。 此外，MARS能够泛化到不同的模型背骨以及仿真和真实机器人实验中，显著改善了WAM推理的效率与性能之间的权衡。 我们的代码可在https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/MARS获取。
